newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks slide on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks slide on U.S. data.

text.p: Madrid stocks lost ground in afternoon trading, pulled lower by losses in U.S. stocks and bonds following a much stronger than expected Chicag purchasing managers index.
* General index down 1.72 points, 0.48 percent, to 353.97.
* Ibex-35 index eased 20.71 points, 0.51 percent, to 4,025.47.

* Telefonica was up five pesetas to 2,325 after announcing first half net profit rose 19.5 percent to 71.88 billion pesetas, in line with expectations. Repsol lost 45 pesetas to 4,065 following lacklustre results on Thursday.

MADRID, Aug 30 (Reuter) - Madrid stocks lost ground in afternoon trading on Friday, pulled lower by losses in U.S. stocks and bonds following a much stronger than expected Chicag purchasing managers index.
The general index was down 1.72 points, 0.48 percent, to 353.97. The Ibex-35 leading share index eased 20.71 points, 0.51 percent, to 4,025.47.

Telefonica was up five pesetas to 2,325 after announcing first half net profit rose 19.5 percent to 71.88 billion pesetas, in line with expectations. Repsol lost 45 pesetas to 4,065 following lacklustre results on Thursday.
"It's been a variable session," said a trader. "It started with losses but during the morning it looked as if the direction was changing. But after the U.S. data uncertainty has returned."
The August Chicago PMI came in at 60.0 percent, much stronger than the 51.9 expected by the market. This made a rise in U.S. rates all but inevitable, traders said.
Volume was 25.8 billion pesetas, with Telefonica, Iberdrola, Repsol and Endesa the most actively traded shares.
Among large banks, Santander fell 20 pesetas to 6,420 while BBV fell 30 to 5,260.
